ideas.title: One cell in a clam shell, and my beak shakes the bubbles off
ideas.critique: This is round 1's clam-shell cell again, now without the side-by-side bench. One cell kept alive by Lumi's own beak is the right fix. Faraday-rate bubble nucleation that raises the resistance is real road step 2 and every later step runs on it. The risk is real numbers: if the metals' EMF and polarisation are typed in for copper/iron only, it is a one-case rig, and if the glow sinks and returns too evenly, the shake plays as a reset button.

ideas.title: The wire I drew burns out where I rushed it
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
same_form: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: This is round 1's drawing idea plus a payoff. It is strong only if the payoff happens: the thin stretch you rushed is where it glows later, and that ties a craft to a consequence through circuit.jl. Sachs stress against Hollomon hardening is a real, reusable law. The hauling shot alone is the old 'tool works a material close up' form, and if the bright spot never appears in the same film, it is a pull-or-snap meter.

ideas.title: I crank, and the light pushes back
ideas.critique: This is round 1's crank idea with the missing coupling added: a Hill muscle driving the crank, so Lumi's strain comes from the real load. That turns the energy loop into a body you watch working, which nothing on the island has done. It depends on the motor actually running first (the last post stuck), and if the pose strain is a blend driven by a number instead of the torque balance, it collapses into a gauge with feathers.

ideas.title: Copper grows on a nail
same_form: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Cementation is real chemistry, and a time-lapse of a colour change is a clean picture. But as a film it is one object changing slowly in a bowl with a fixed view, and the colour-from-concentration and rates will likely be fitted constants for malachite and vinegar alone. It is step 9, the road's far end, while steps 1 to 5 still don't work.

ideas.title: My first light, carried through the dark
ideas.critique: This is round 1's bulb with the critique's warning taken: a moving light that walks past the friends' faces, which is a real use of path tracing and a sharable picture. But it depends on a cell, a circuit, a blown bulb and drawn wire all existing, so the likeliest made version types in a filament temperature. The failure mid-walk risks being timed for drama rather than coming from the oxide growth.

ideas.title: The wire's song
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: A wire that hums from I x B resonance is the only idea here that is heard, and tuning by tension is a real mechanic. But it needs the cranked AC generator, which does not exist, so it most likely ends up as a string driven at a typed frequency. The solved-note-of-an-object payoff has been done twice already (the stone, the lantern), and it is a side branch of the cart.
